item.title: Baldwin County's Miss AWAG pageant marks 30 years of building young women
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: A pageant that's been a fixture in Baldwin County for three decades is celebrating its milestone while continuing its mission to do far more than crown a winner each year. The Miss Area Women Action Group Pageant has provided a platform for young women across Baldwin County since its inception, according to WKRG News 5. But organizers say the real…
item.content:encoded:
A pageant that's been a fixture in Baldwin County for three decades is celebrating its milestone while continuing its mission to do far more than crown a winner each year.

The Miss Area Women Action Group Pageant has provided a platform for young women across Baldwin County since its inception, according to WKRG News 5. But organizers say the real value extends well beyond the stage—the competition focuses on building confidence, leadership skills, and community involvement among participants.

For 30 years, the pageant has offered contestants an opportunity to develop personal growth and make connections in their community. The emphasis on substance over pure pageantry has allowed the event to remain relevant and meaningful to the young women who compete, even as entertainment and youth programs have evolved dramatically over the decades.

The Miss AWAG pageant's longevity in Baldwin County reflects the broader appeal of programs that balance competition with personal development for young adults.

item.content:encoded:
A teenager was killed in a crash on Interstate 65 in Conecuh County, Alabama on Sunday evening, according to the Conecuh County Coroner's Office. The single-vehicle crash occurred just before 9:30 p.m. on September 13.

Details about the circumstances of the crash, the teen's identity, and what led to the collision have not yet been released. The coroner's office is continuing its investigation into the fatal accident.

If you witnessed the crash or have information about the incident, authorities encourage you to contact the Conecuh County Sheriff's Office.

item.content:encoded:
Drivers across Escambia and Santa Rosa counties should prepare for traffic slowdowns as road crews continue construction and maintenance work on several major corridors this week.

According to reports from the area, Interstate 10 resurfacing work east of U.S. 231 is among the projects creating potential delays for commuters. The work is part of ongoing efforts to maintain and improve the roadway infrastructure serving the region.

Motoristas are urged to allow extra time for their commutes and exercise caution in construction zones. The specific hours of work and exact closure locations may vary by day, so checking current traffic conditions before heading out is recommended.

For the most up-to-date information on road construction schedules and alternate routes, drivers can contact the Florida Department of Transportation or check local traffic reports.

item.title: Florida Gas Prices Climb Above $4 a Gallon Again
item.dc:creator: newsroom

The uptick reflects broader pressure from rising oil prices, which continue to push gasoline costs higher at stations statewide. Pensacola-area drivers filling up should…
item.content:encoded:
Drivers across Florida are seeing pump prices surge above the $4 mark once again, marking the first time since early June that gas has climbed to this level, according to AAA.

The uptick reflects broader pressure from rising oil prices, which continue to push gasoline costs higher at stations statewide. Pensacola-area drivers filling up should expect to see similar increases reflected locally as wholesale prices continue climbing.

AAA tracks price movements daily, and the current jump comes after a period of relatively lower prices over the past several months. Motorists looking to save money may want to check apps that track local pump prices, as rates can vary between stations.

item.title: Hot, Dry Start to Week; Weekend Rain Expected in NW Florida
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: The Pensacola area is bracing for a hot, dry stretch early this week before moisture returns by the weekend, according to the National Weather Service forecast for North Escambia County. Monday will be sunny with highs near 92 degrees and calm winds, with overnight lows settling around 73. Tuesday looks even hotter, with highs climbing to 93 and…
item.content:encoded:
The Pensacola area is bracing for a hot, dry stretch early this week before moisture returns by the weekend, according to the National Weather Service forecast for North Escambia County.

Monday will be sunny with highs near 92 degrees and calm winds, with overnight lows settling around 73. Tuesday looks even hotter, with highs climbing to 93 and heat index values climbing as high as 106 degrees. Winds will remain light, becoming easterly at around 5 mph in the afternoon.

The mostly clear conditions are expected to persist into Tuesday night. Residents are advised to stay hydrated and take precautions during the hottest part of the day, especially with heat index values approaching dangerous levels midweek.

Rain chances are forecast to rebound by the weekend, which could provide some relief from the intense heat and dry conditions expected early in the week.

item.title: Molino Community Center Closing Next Week for Historic Floor Restoration
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: The Molino Community Center and its attached library will shut down for a week starting Saturday, September 19, to restore the building's vintage flooring. The closure runs through Saturday, September 26, according to county officials. The work is part of an ongoing effort to preserve the character of the facility, which was originally built as…
item.content:encoded:
The Molino Community Center and its attached library will shut down for a week starting Saturday, September 19, to restore the building's vintage flooring.

The closure runs through Saturday, September 26, according to county officials. The work is part of an ongoing effort to preserve the character of the facility, which was originally built as Molino School back in 1939.

Patrons should plan ahead during the closure, as both the community center and library services will be unavailable. The museum housed at the location will also be closed during this period. Officials haven't announced whether the restored floors will reopen ahead of schedule if work finishes early.

item.title: Free Meals for All Students at 44 Escambia County Schools This Year
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Escambia County Schools is offering free breakfast and lunch to every student at 44 schools and centers during the 2024-2025 school year, regardless of family income. The expanded meal program means families won't need to submit applications or make payments at those participating locations. However, families with students at 11 other Escambia…
item.content:encoded:
Escambia County Schools is offering free breakfast and lunch to every student at 44 schools and centers during the 2024-2025 school year, regardless of family income. The expanded meal program means families won't need to submit applications or make payments at those participating locations.

However, families with students at 11 other Escambia County schools will still need to either submit applications for free or reduced-price meals, or pay for lunch as usual. School officials encourage parents to check which schools fall into each category to understand what their family needs to do.

The free meal program is designed to ensure all students have access to nutritious breakfast and lunch throughout the school day, removing potential barriers to participation. Parents with questions about which schools offer universal free meals or how to apply at other locations can contact their child's school directly.

item.content:encoded:
A man was airlifted to a hospital Sunday evening following a serious ATV accident in the Walnut Hill area. According to witnesses, the adult male was traveling southbound on Highway 97 just south of South Highway 99 when his ATV suddenly veered off the roadway and into a nearby driveway.

The crash left the rider in critical condition, prompting emergency responders to call for helicopter transport to a trauma center. The exact cause of the sudden veering remains under investigation.

Florida Highway Patrol and local emergency services responded to the scene. The incident underscores ongoing safety concerns about recreational vehicle use on North Escambia roadways.

item.title: Florida Leaders Ramp Up Push Against Tech Companies, Terrorism as Campaign Season Intensifies
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Florida government officials are stepping up efforts on two major fronts as the political season shifts into higher gear following the Labor Day holiday, according to reporting from North Escambia. State leaders have increased their focus on regulating technology companies and combating terrorism threats, with lawmakers signaling that artificial…
item.content:encoded:
Florida government officials are stepping up efforts on two major fronts as the political season shifts into higher gear following the Labor Day holiday, according to reporting from North Escambia.

State leaders have increased their focus on regulating technology companies and combating terrorism threats, with lawmakers signaling that artificial intelligence will be a central concern going forward. "AI is only going to get more advanced," one official noted, underscoring expectations that tech regulation will remain a priority issue heading into the fall.

The push comes as political campaigns across Florida have resumed after the summer pause, bringing renewed attention to policy positions and legislative priorities. The dual emphasis on tech oversight and security reflects broader national debates about innovation, regulation, and public safety that are playing out in state capitals across the country.

For North Florida residents, these state-level initiatives could have ripple effects on everything from cybersecurity protections to how emerging technologies are deployed in schools, workplaces, and government services.

The Pensacola Blue Wahoos absorbed a lopsided 19-1 loss to the Biloxi Shuckers on Saturday night in one of their final regular-season games. According to the game report, Wahoos pitchers struggled significantly, issuing 12 walks while allowing 15 hits as Biloxi dominated the matchup.

The blowout appeared to serve as a low-leverage opportunity for several pitchers to get work in advance of the postseason. Ian Lewis Jr. was among the players who saw action in the game.

The loss sets up the Blue Wahoos' final games of the regular season as they prepare for playoff positioning. Despite the lopsided defeat, the team will look to regroup before the postseason stretch begins.

item.content:encoded:
A Cantonment man has been sentenced following an April 2026 incident that endangered a child, according to North Escambia reporting.

Colton David Gideons, 27, pleaded no contest to charges of child abuse without great bodily harm, simple assault with domestic violence enhancement, and reckless driving. Authorities say Gideons threatened a woman and forced her vehicle off the road while a child was inside the car.

The sentencing follows the incidents detailed in the initial investigation. Court records indicate Gideons' actions put the child at risk during the confrontation on the roadway.

item.title: Molino Woman Enters Pretrial Diversion in Amusement Park Burglary Case

Madison Lee Galle was charged in February with unarmed burglary of an unoccupied structure and criminal mischief, both felonies. The charges stemmed from…
item.content:encoded:
A 19-year-old Molino woman accused of burglarizing a local waterpark and amusement park where she once worked has agreed to a deferred prosecution arrangement, according to court records.

Madison Lee Galle was charged in February with unarmed burglary of an unoccupied structure and criminal mischief, both felonies. The charges stemmed from break-ins at facilities in the North Escambia area where Galle had previously been employed.

Under the pretrial diversion agreement, Galle can avoid prosecution if she meets the terms set by the court. If successfully completed, the charges would typically be dismissed and the arrest record may be eligible for expungement.

Pretrial diversion programs are commonly used in cases involving first-time offenders or situations where rehabilitation may be more appropriate than traditional prosecution.

item.content:encoded:
A brief window for rain wraps up this weekend as North Escambia prepares for a hot, dry stretch ahead. Sunday offers only a 30 percent chance of scattered showers and thunderstorms, mainly after 1 p.m., with highs near 91 degrees and mostly sunny skies otherwise, according to the National Weather Service forecast.

Starting Monday, the region shifts into a notably hotter and drier pattern. Afternoon temperatures are expected to climb around 90 degrees daily with little to no rain expected through at least the early part of the week. Residents should prepare for sustained heat and limited precipitation relief, making it a good time to ensure adequate hydration and account for increased cooling needs.

item.title: Escambia Schools May Close Buildings, Rezone as District Starts 'Right-Sizing' Review
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: The Escambia County Public Schools District is launching a significant review of its infrastructure that could reshape how schools are assigned and potentially close underutilized facilities. The School Attendance Zone Advisory Committee will hold its first meeting this month to tackle what the district calls a "right-sizing" initiative. According…
item.content:encoded:
The Escambia County Public Schools District is launching a significant review of its infrastructure that could reshape how schools are assigned and potentially close underutilized facilities. The School Attendance Zone Advisory Committee will hold its first meeting this month to tackle what the district calls a "right-sizing" initiative.

According to North Escambia, the committee will convene September 24 at the Vernon McDaniel Building on Pace Boulevard to begin examining school attendance zones and facility usage. The process could result in realigning attendance boundaries, rezoning existing schools, or permanently closing buildings that don't serve current enrollment needs.

The right-sizing effort reflects broader challenges facing school districts across Florida as enrollment patterns shift and aging facilities strain budgets. The committee's work will likely generate significant interest from families concerned about which schools might close or see boundary changes.

Parents and community members interested in the process are expected to be able to weigh in as the committee progresses through its review over the coming months.

The victim was taken to a Mobile hospital with non-life-threatening injuries to his upper leg. A school bus with children on board happened to be driving through the area during the shooting, though no kids…
item.content:encoded:
Bay Minette, AL (NewsRadio 92.3) -- Bay Minette Police say a 17-year-old boy shot an 18-year-old man Thursday afternoon near Newport Parkway. The victim was taken to a Mobile hospital with non-life-threatening injuries to his upper leg.


A school bus with children on board happened to be driving through the area during the shooting, though no kids were hurt.


Police are also charging a fifteen-year-old with possessing a stolen gun after determining he wasn't connected to the shooting itself. A twenty-three-year-old man detained alongside the teen shooter is still being questioned.
